prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: one square ability-card illustration for a serious fantasy game.
Input images: Image 1 is the Magic Missile EDIT TARGET and composition/paint template. Image 2 is the approved Spirit Slash supporting STYLE REFERENCE only.
Primary request: edit Image 1 into the new ability illustration described below. Remove both ivory missiles and all their blue seeking ribbons completely. Replace the entire foreground subject with the new subject. Keep the same coarse matte gouache vocabulary as both references: wide visible brush marks, rough simple painted shapes, flat shadow planes, loose edges, atmospheric arches and warm amber depth. The result must look painted by the same artist and at the same intentionally coarse finish, not a more refined HD variation.
Scene/backdrop: preserve the reference's inhabited architectural atmosphere with loosely painted stone arches, steps, warm amber air and restrained candlelight. Keep real depth behind the subject, never bare paper or a studio void. The scene is neutral and inviting enough to read as an ability, not evil. No enemy, villain, monster, sinister face or antagonist behind it.
Composition: square; new ability subject is the sole clear focus, fits within the central 70% of the image, and reads at 40px. Keep the lower 20% calmer for a card fade. No card borders, letters, labels, logos or text.
Avoid: photorealism, HD rendering, realistic surface textures, polished/glossy objects, smooth gradients, lens effects, bokeh, bloom, intricate engraving, microscopic ornament, sci-fi machinery, paper-only backgrounds. Broad strokes and simple shading must remain visible. Preserve the reference's visual weight and coarse detail level.
Subject: a worn simple talisman suspended from a loose cord in the foreground, a roughly painted bronze-and-ivory charm with a single quiet lucky gleam. Give it a distinctive uncomplicated four-point form, with the gleam as a small warm amber accent. It should suggest favorable chance and quiet protection, not a jewelry product photograph. Keep the shape large and readable with coarse matte edges and almost no ornamental detail.
